prompt: A union-bound proof finds one random string that makes an amplified BPP algorithm correct on every input of a given length. What has it established?

options.text: A non-uniform advice string exists; finding it efficiently has not been shown
options.explanation: Correct. The proof supplies a polynomial-size string for each length, but is not an efficient construction.
Advice existence does not produce a uniform deterministic algorithm.

options.text: One fixed string works for every input length
options.explanation: Different input lengths can require different advice strings.

options.text: BPP is contained in NP by treating any accepting random string as a certificate
options.explanation: BPP may accept no-instances on some strings, so that certificate argument works for RP and does not establish BPP in NP.

workedExample:
1. Amplify the per-input error enough that the sum over all inputs of one length is below one.
2. At least one random string therefore succeeds on all those inputs.
3. Hard-wire that string as advice for this length.
4. No efficient search for the string follows, so P versus BPP remains open.
